title: Students' Knowledge of Personalised Learning: How AI Can Help?
content:
This study assessed 450 Malaysian secondary school students' understanding of personalised learning, revealing that students strongly associate it with teacher-directed differentiation but poorly understand learner autonomy, self-pacing, and digital facilitation. AI-powered platforms are proposed as direct and indirect interventions to bridge this conceptual gap and support self-regulated learning.


ABSTRACT

Personalised learning aims to align instruction with students' needs, interests, and motivation through responsive learning environments. However, many students demonstrate limited understanding of this concept, often associating it only with self-paced learning or technology use. Such misconceptions weaken classroom implementation and may reduce student engagement and self-regulation. This study aims to calibrate students' understanding of personalised learning and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can be leveraged, directly and indirectly, to address key areas of misunderstanding and enhance effective implementation. The study involved 450 high school students aged 16–18 from selected schools in Kedah, Penang, and Perak, using a purposive sampling approach. Data were collected through a questionnaire administered during class after participants were briefed on the concept of personalised learning and the study purpose. Validity and reliability of the assessed constructs were evaluated using factor loadings (λ), average variance extracted (AVE), Cronbach's alpha (α), and composite reliability (CR), with acceptable thresholds of λ > 0.50, AVE > 0.50, α > 0.60, and CR > 0.60. Students' knowledge scores were analysed to identify aspects of personalised learning that were well understood and those requiring further clarification, providing an empirical basis for targeted instructional interventions. The findings indicate that the measurement model demonstrated adequate reliability and validity. Students strongly associated personalised learning with needs-based differentiation, particularly in project-based and mixed-ability contexts, but showed weaker understanding of learner autonomy, self-paced learning, and digital facilitation. These results reveal a conceptual gap between theory and practice. Practical AI-based strategies are proposed to enhance learning effectiveness and support adaptive, self-regulated learning environments.
